title: Non-blocking finding from frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups' PR review (#404)
description: pr-reviewer's full review of PR #404 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups) accepted it -- make e2e (28/28, plus a mutation test that temporarily broke the History table's date rendering to confirm the assertion is still load-bearing), static analysis, and coverage all passed, and the waitForResponse-vs-click ordering was verified correct (listener registered before the triggering click via Promise.all, not after). One non-blocking test-infrastructure-convention finding surfaced and shouldn't disappear once PR #404 merges.

checklist.step: frontend/tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts now imports directly from `../../src/api/homework` (a type) and `../../src/utils/format` (a value) -- the first e2e spec in frontend/tests/e2e/ to import anything from `src/` at all; every other spec that needs a shared helper (e.g. portfolio.spec.ts's `isoDateWeeksAgo`) imports it from `tests/dateFixtures.ts` instead, a tests-local module, not application source. This import is correct and was the right fix for the specific duplication finding it closed (the task's checklist explicitly called for importing `formatDate` directly), but it's a new precedent: an e2e spec now has a compile-time dependency on an app-source module's exact path/export shape, which couples a black-box browser-level test to an internal refactor in a way the rest of the suite doesn't. Worth an explicit, recorded convention decision for future specs -- e.g. should an e2e spec import src/ helpers directly when there's no real alternative (as here), or should a shared tests/-local re-export/wrapper be preferred to keep that coupling at one boundary -- rather than leaving it as an ad hoc one-off that future spec authors might copy inconsistently.
